Nipissing First Nation

Nipissing First Nation’s public sources connect Nbisiing language and historical learning with continuing responsibilities to Lake Nipissing. The Culture Centre’s account and a joint statement with Dokis offer two complementary ways into community knowledge and stewardship.

01

Learning through community archives and living knowledge

Nipissing’s Culture Centre describes its work as restoring the Nbisiing dialect and strengthening cultural and historical learning. Its public account brings together archival documents, photographs, earlier interviews and conversations with elders. Hockey history and the Nipissing Indian Homemakers Club appear among its research initiatives. These are community-led routes into history; the linked books, recordings and exhibits require their own inspection.

Read the sources [1] Nipissing First Nation

02

Working with Dokis across connected waters

In their September 2026 statement, Nipissing and Dokis describe linked families, histories and responsibilities to Lake Nipissing and the French River. They announce a joint committee for shared stewardship priorities. This is a dated statement of intention, not evidence that every proposed activity has since been completed.

Read the sources [2] Nipissing First Nation and Dokis First Nation
